paper.title: Comparison of robustness to outliers between robust poisson models and log-binomial models when estimating relative risks for common binary outcomes: a simulation study
paper.citation: Chen W, Shi J, Qian L, Azen SP. Comparison of robustness to outliers between robust poisson models and log-binomial models when estimating relative risks for common binary outcomes: a simulation study. BMC Medical Research Methodology 14:82 (2014)

items.label: Additional file 1, the 24 scenarios: exposure 50% and outcome 10, 25 or 40%

assumptions.what: P(X = 1) and P(Y = 1) are computed by quadrature over Z ~ Beta(6, 2) from the alpha0 and beta0 printed in Additional file 1
assumptions.sensitivity: Exact up to quadrature; the largest p_y of any scenario is 0.944, so p_y never exceeds 1 and no rule for p_y > 1 is needed.

items.label: Table 1, relative bias (%) of the log RR, n = 1500 (18 rows x 8 cells)

assumptions.what: Contamination flips the outcome of the records whose true p_y lies beyond the population's rate/2 and 1 - rate/2 quantiles of p_y (computed exactly for each scenario), so the number flipped varies between data sets (74.9 on average at 5% and n = 1500, SD 8.5). The paper says only 'p_y at bottom or top 1%' (2.5% for 5%)
assumptions.sensitivity: Two readings tested on every contaminated cell. Flipping exactly ceil(n rate/2) records per tail in every data set (76 at 5%, n = 1500) leaves the n = 1500 means where they are (Table 1: 96 of 96 within tolerance) but makes the SEs too small at outcome 10% and 5% contamination (Table 2: 89 of 96, Table A2: 87 of 96 within tolerance, against 96 and 96 with population cut-offs), and at n = 500 it moves the biases of RR 2.0, outcome 10%, non-linear strong (Table A1: 92 of 96, against 96).

assumptions.what: Both tails are flipped (2%: the bottom 1% and the top 1% of p_y)
assumptions.sensitivity: The whole rate flipped at the bottom gives 3 of 96 contaminated cells of Table 1 within tolerance, at the top 0; both tails 96.

assumptions.what: Records are ranked by the true p_y of the generating model
assumptions.sensitivity: Ranking by p_y fitted by the uncontaminated log-binomial model (a fixed number per data set) gives 85 of 96 contaminated cells of Table 1 within tolerance and 79 of Table 3.

assumptions.what: The fitted models include Z^2 when the confounder is quadratic (the Discussion speaks of 'the higher-order term of Z' added into the model; the Methods do not say)
assumptions.sensitivity: Leaving Z^2 out gives 50 of 72 non-linear cells of Table 1 within tolerance and 56 of Table 3, against 72 and 72 with it.

assumptions.what: The log-binomial fit reported is the maximum likelihood fit when it lies inside the parameter space, else the COPY fit with C = 1,000,000 (weights C on the data, 1 on the data with the outcome reversed); our solver is Newton's method with a line search, not SAS GENMOD
assumptions.sensitivity: When the maximum is interior the COPY fit equals it to O(1/C), so the switching rule does not move the estimates. Our fits equal an independent maximizer's: 60 contaminated data sets (8 COPY fits): robust Poisson coefficients equal statsmodels' to 1.2e-12 and the sandwich SE its HC0 SE to a relative 3.1e-12; log-binomial coefficients equal an independent maximizer's to 1.0e-06, with a likelihood at least as high (to 1.1e-13) and a score of at most 4.0e-06.

assumptions.what: Random numbers: NumPy's PCG64 with fixed seeds per scenario; the paper's SAS seeds are not given
assumptions.sensitivity: A second run with other seeds puts 863 of 864 printed cells within tolerance.

assumptions.what: The alpha0 and beta0 of Additional file 1 are used for n = 500 too
assumptions.sensitivity: Not varied; Tables A1-A3 come back at 144, 144 and 144 of 144 cells.

assumptions.what: The empirical SE uses the divisor 999 and the MSE is the squared mean error plus that variance
assumptions.sensitivity: The divisor 1,000 changes an SE by 0.05% of its value, far below the printed precision.

items.label: Fig. 1A, relative bias, linear Z, moderate association (n = 1500)

cause.summary: Ours scores 0.958 against a pass mark of 0.95; the best wrong input scores 0.175 and the best near miss 0.736. At 2 px a pixel score cannot resolve Monte Carlo noise: one point of relative bias is 4.62 px, and the Monte Carlo SE of a 1,000-replicate relative bias is 0.3 to 1.3 points. Two runs of our own simulation with different seeds score only 0.741 against each other in this panel, while the paper's own Table 1 drawn with the same code scores 0.983, so the drawing and the frame are right. The values behind the panel are Table 1: its 36 values for this panel are each within tolerance and sit at an RMS z of 0.43 from the paper's, where our two runs sit at 0.84 from each other.

exceptions.evidence: The paper prints 0.013. Its own Tables 1 and 2 give this cell a relative bias of -23.7% and an SE of 0.09, which make an MSE of 0.0351 (computed in comparison.json, consistency); the robust Poisson cell next to it prints 0.035. Ours is 0.0357 (second run 0.0341). 141 of the 144 MSEs of Table 3 agree with the paper's own bias and SE at their printed precision. Besides this one, 2 more do not (RR 1.5, 25%, 0%: linear moderate, LB prints 0.008 against 0.0090 to 0.0110; RR 1.5, 25%, 0%: linear moderate, RP prints 0.008 against 0.0090 to 0.0110); ours is within tolerance of the printed value in each.
